data.title: India vows action after first cheetah shot dead
data.description: NEW DELHI — India has vowed "swift action" after a cheetah was shot dead, the first such killing since the country began reintroducing the animals in 2022, the government said Wednesday.

data.title: S.African activists push back on data centre rush
data.description: CAPE TOWN — A little boy balanced a large bottle of water on his shoulder as he returned from a communal tap near land acquired by a major data centre developer in South Africa's water-scarce city of Cape Town.

data.title: 200 ‘cruise for life’ passengers stranded in Cambodia
data.description: Around 200 passengers who paid to live on a cruise ship while travelling the world were abruptly left in a Cambodian port after the company ran out of money, an official said on Wednesday.

data.title: Asean envoy to lead humanitarian mission to Myanmar
data.description: MANILA — ⁠The ⁠Association of Southeast Asian Nations' (Asean) ​special envoy on Myanmar will lead a ​humanitarian mission to the ‌country starting on Wednesday, Asean chair the Philippines said.

data.title: 'Now or Never': Ethiopia influencers push for Eritrea invasion
data.description: ADDIS ABABA - Ethiopian online influencers are pushing for their government to invade neighbouring Eritrea and seize access to the sea, following its success against rebel and Eritrean forces in recent weeks.

data.title: Judges set to rule on Australian mushroom killer's appeal
data.description: SYDNEY - Australian mushroom murderer Erin Patterson will learn Friday if she has succeeded in overturning her conviction for killing three people with a poisoned beef Wellington lunch.

data.title: Iran war cost rises to $47.1 billion, Pentagon told lawmakers
data.description: WASHINGTON — The cost of the war in Iran rose to US$47.1 billion through Oct 16, with bombs, missiles and other munitions accounting for more than 60% of the expenses, the Pentagon told Congress last week. Even with President Donald Trump holding back on restarting major combat operations, at least for now, the Pentagon still incurred about $3.5 billion in additional costs in the roughly six weeks since the Pentagon shared estimates with lawmakers last month.

data.title: Runners swap streets for shopping malls as haze chokes Singapore
data.description: SINGAPORE - The pounding of running shoes echoes through a Singapore shopping mall as fitness enthusiasts desperate to exercise take refuge from choking haze.

data.title: UK set for cautious budget as borrowing costs climb
data.description: LONDON - Britain's finance minister John Healey has readied to unveil his first budget Wednesday, as he juggles commitments to defence spending and easing household bills with little financial room to manoeuvre.

data.title: Trump tamed after US midterms? Europe doubts it
data.description: BRUSSELS (BELGIUM) - President Donald Trump may be facing a political pounding at the US midterm elections next month — but in Europe expectations are low that a big Democrat win would change much.

data.title: Tuvalu has ''limited' power to halt its fossil fuel investments: NZ govt papers seen by AFP
data.description: SYDNEY - A low-lying Pacific nation urging drastic climate action has "limited ability" to halt its own government investments in fossil fuel companies, external advisers wrote in internal documents obtained by AFP.

data.title: Palestinian activist Khalil returns to Columbia after US detention
data.description: NEW YORK - Mahmoud Khalil, a figurehead of Gaza war protests in the United States, returned on Tuesday to Columbia University for the first time since his 2025 arrest under President Donald Trump's crackdown on pro-Palestinian activists.

data.title: In tight Israel vote, both camps hold out cautious hope
data.description: TEL AVIV - As the first exit polls arrived in Israel's election, opposition supporters breathed a sigh of relief. But as a long night set in, nervousness grew on both sides in a tight race that is pivotal for the country.

data.title: Trump drastically loosens oil and gas methane rules
data.description: LUBBOCK (UNITED STATES) - US President Donald Trump announced on Tuesday a sweeping rollback of rules that stop oil and gas producers from emitting methane, a greenhouse gas super pollutant.

data.title: India evacuates tens of thousands as Cyclone Arnab makes landfall
data.description: KAKINADA (INDIA) - Ferocious winds and torrential rain lashed India's southeastern coast as Cyclone Arnab made landfall on Wednesday, forcing nearly 100,000 people to evacuate their homes in two states, authorities said.

data.title: 'They don't care about us': Trump food aid cuts leave Americans struggling and angry
data.description: TUCSON - Christine, a retired widow in Arizona, placed food staples in her cart at a charity food distribution event — as she's had to do monthly since the Trump administration slashed federal food assistance programmes.

data.title: AI chip giant SK hynix says quarterly operating profit soars 630%
data.description: SEOUL - South Korean chip giant SK hynix said Wednesday its third-quarter operating profit soared 632 percent on-year, largely driven by the artificial intelligence industry's explosive demand for its advanced memory chips.

data.title: French Senate weighs bill to make protesters pay for unrest damage
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - The French parliament's upper house on Tuesday debated a controversial bill that would make protesters financially liable for damage caused during street demonstrations, despite warnings from critics that it could curb the right to protest.

data.title: American woman convicted of getting military training from Islamic State
data.description: NEW YORK - An American woman who joined the Islamic State group before being caught by anti-IS forces in Syria was found guilty on Tuesday of receiving military training from the jihadists.

data.title: UN nuclear watchdog chief urges Iran to grant access
data.description: UNITED NATIONS (UNITED STATES) - IAEA chief Rafael Grossi urged Iran during a UN Security Council meeting on Tuesday to grant immediate access to his agency so it can verify the Islamic republic's nuclear materials.

data.title: Syria condemns deadly Jordan strikes as 'unacceptable violation'
data.description: DAMASCUS - Syria condemned on Tuesday deadly strikes on the country's south a day earlier that Jordan said killed more than 20 jihadists as retaliation for a gun attack on a church.

data.title: UK charges two men with security offences in airbase plot
data.description: LONDON - UK anti-terrorism police said on Tuesday that two men have been charged with national security offences after an incident last month at a British airbase used by the United States, linking the scare to Iran.

data.title: EU seeks deportation powers for beefed-up border agency
data.description: BRUSSELS - The European Union wants to give its border agency greater powers, including handling deportations, under plans to strengthen the bloc’s response to irregular migration presented on Tuesday.

data.title: UK man ‘offered drugged wife to strangers online for sex’
data.description: WINCHESTER, England - A British man who drugged and raped his then-wife over 13 years had advertised online for strangers to have sex with her without her consent, a court heard on Tuesday.

data.title: Greenhouse gas levels ‘hit record highs in 2025’
data.description: GENEVA - Greenhouse gas concentrations in the atmosphere rose to record highs in 2025, locking in climate impacts that will persist for centuries to come, the United Nations said on Tuesday.

data.title: Norwegian, Finnish leaders hold ‘frank’ talks with Putin
data.description: HELSINKI - The Finnish president and Norwegian prime minister held a “frank and substantive” discussion with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Tuesday about efforts to end the war in Ukraine, the Nordic leaders said.

data.title: Japan sets 'second capital' criteria, 4 prefectures qualify
data.description: The Japanese government approved an ordinance on Tuesday setting requirements for designation as a "second capital" to back up Tokyo in disasters and promote decentralisation, with Osaka and three other prefectures qualifying.

data.title: Reparations calls overshadow King Charles’ Caribbean trip
data.description: LONDON - King Charles III begins a delicate tour of the Caribbean on Tuesday, overshadowed by calls to apologise and pay reparations for the slave trade, which he has called the “darkest days” of British history.

data.title: Myanmar refugee in Denmark demands justice over junta war crimes
data.description: A Myanmar citizen living in Denmark on Monday filed a complaint with Danish authorities against the country’s ruling military junta for alleged war crimes committed against minorities.

data.title: Israel to give verdict on Netanyahu in pivotal election
data.description: JERUSALEM - A deeply divided Israel will head to the polls on Tuesday for the first time since Hamas's attack on Oct 7, 2023, with voters delivering their verdict on veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the country's rightward drift.

data.title: In Israel, Eisenkot tries quiet appeal to oust Netanyahu
data.description: JERUSALEM - Gadi Eisenkot, the man who could unseat Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, almost always dresses in black, speaks halting English and tends to respond in interviews with bullet-point lists, a reflection of the military culture that shaped him.

data.title: New Zealand ex-PM Ardern to teach leadership in Sydney
data.description: SYDNEY — Former New Zealand prime minister Jacinda Ardern will teach students about "empathetic leadership" after being hired for a new job at the University of Sydney.

data.title: $1m bounties, dawn arrests: Trump presses voter fraud campaign
data.description: LOS ANGELES — As the United States heads toward November's midterms, US President Donald Trump and Republicans are issuing increasingly dire warnings of voter fraud, while Democrats and voting-rights activists mobilise against what they call a campaign of intimidation designed to scare people away from the ballot box.

data.title: Benjamin Netanyahu: Israel's longest-serving PM fighting for survival
data.description: JERUSALEM — Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's consummate political survivor, faces the fight of his life in Tuesday's election as he tries to convince voters he is still the only candidate capable of keeping them safe.

data.title: HK Express passenger injured after power bank overheats on flight to Jeju
data.description: A traveller was injured after a power bank overheated and emitted smoke aboard an HK Express flight from Hong Kong to South Korea on Sunday, prompting crew members to deploy emergency safety measures before the aircraft landed safely.

data.title: US-brokered truce begins in Ukraine city occupied by Russia
data.description: KYIV, Ukraine - A truce between Ukraine and Russia aimed at allowing humanitarian aid into the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky entered into force early on Tuesday, having been announced by US First Lady Melania Trump last week.

data.title: Lula win rattles Brazil markets over spending spree fears
data.description: RIO DE JANEIRO (BRAZIL) - The reelection of Brazilian leftist Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva rattled markets on Monday as investors, who had expected a win for his conservative rival, worried about fiscal discipline.

data.title: Brazilian lawmaker Andre Janones, Lula's social media 'general'
data.description: SAO PAULO - In Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's first victory speech, he praised "our general" Andre Janones, the brains behind the online campaign that ensured his stunning comeback.

data.title: Netanyahu, rivals trade attacks over Iran as clock counts down to Israel vote
data.description: JERUSALEM - Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu wrapped up his campaign to remain in power on Monday with a claim that Israel faced potential annihilation at the hands of Iran should his election rivals prevail.
